# Module overview {#sec-m1-visao-geral}

::: {.modulo-meta}
**Workload:** 6 hours (3h synchronous + 3h asynchronous)\
**Dates:** 28/09 and 01/10 (synchronous); 02/10 (asynchronous)\
**Data used:** ANTAQ coastal shipping (TKU 2025), Comex Stat and an export of the Curitiba metropolitan region's four-step model (PTV VISUM)
:::

## What you will be able to do by the end of the module

- Install and organise an R analysis project that someone else can run again.
- Read spreadsheets and heavy text files, and export results as `.csv` and `.xlsx`.
- Handle text (municipality names, port facilities, commodity codes) and dates.
- Filter, group, summarise and reshape tables (*long* ↔ *wide*).
- Diagnose quality problems: *encoding*, duplicates, missing values, *outliers* and
  impossible values.
- Combine different datasets with `join` and know **why** some rows do not match.
- Read the export of a simulation model and check units, sentinel values and totals before
  publishing any indicator.
- Produce publication-quality charts with `ggplot2`.

## Module packages

This is the first module, so the list below is the starting point: every package used from
here on is added to this base, never replaces it. The following modules only list what
is **new** compared with the previous module. Run the block below **once** before the
first class. Installation may take a few minutes.

```{r}
#| eval: false
pacotes <- c(
  # reading and writing
  "readr", "readxl", "writexl", "data.table", "duckplyr",
  # wrangling
  "dplyr", "tidyr", "stringr", "lubridate", "forcats", "janitor",
  # visualisation
  "ggplot2", "scales", "patchwork", "classInt", "ggrepel",
  # reports and reproducibility
  "knitr", "rmarkdown", "renv", "reprex"
)

faltando <- setdiff(pacotes, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(faltando) > 0) install.packages(faltando)
```

To check that everything is in place:

```{r}
#| eval: false
sapply(
  c("dplyr", "tidyr", "stringr", "lubridate", "ggplot2", "readxl"),
  requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE
)
```

## Conventions used in the material

- Code blocks can be run. The output appears right below, preceded by `#>`.
- We use R's native *pipe*, `|>`, available since version 4.1.
- Calls such as `dplyr::filter()` name the package explicitly: it is good practice in
  scripts that other people will read and it avoids name clashes.
- File paths are always **relative to the project root** (`dados/arquivo.csv`),
  never absolute (`C:/Users/...`). That is what lets the script run on any
  colleague's machine.
- Object and column names in the code are in Portuguese, as in the original course
  (`pacotes` = packages, `faltando` = missing, `dados` = data, `resultados` = results).
